title: Oulipoly Exploration v1 Extension
description: Host-selected provider/v1 extension by which a host offers a registered parent agent opaque child route labels, its child requester and the name of its owner ingress variable, as launch-environment data. Selected by host.env.OULIPOLY_HOST_EXPLORATION_V1=1 in describe and advertised as capabilities.exploration_v1. The host places one Exploration object, JSON-encoded, in the launch environment variable OULIPOLY_EXPLORATION_V1 (policy.evaluate launch.env, and so the evaluated and resident template env), only together with oulipoly.tool_mediation/v1. Its absence is no offer: the agent keeps the mediated bash tool alone. The offered tool runs no command; the host's owner admits or refuses every child.

RouteLabel.description: Opaque site route label. It names no provider, model or account to the provider; only the host's owner knows what it launches.

Limits.description: The root's child limits as the host offers them, for the agent's information. The owner's admission is authoritative and may refuse sooner.

requester.description: Absolute path of the host's child requester. It implements the root-child v1 requester surface: `REQUESTER ROUTE PROMPT` asks the owner named by ingress_env for one child on ROUTE and keeps the request open while the child lives; stdout is one JSON object: the owner's final `result` (exit 0) or `refused` (exit 65), or `lost` (exit 75: the request may have reached the owner); exit 69 means no ingress or the owner was unreachable before anything was sent and exit 64 refused arguments, both with nothing sent; stderr may relay the owner's stage lines as `LABEL: JSON`.

ingress_env.description: Name of the environment variable through which the host names the owner's ingress to the serving process and its descendants. It is not part of this object's value; without it no requester starts.

EffectiveExploration.description: Value of the oulipoly.exploration/v1 policy.evaluate marker: what the provider will configure natively for this offer. tool is the exploration tool's native name, which the tool-mediation marker's native_tools also lists. Construction, not a certificate that the native CLI honours it.
